section: Minor dynasties of Andhradesa - Chalukya-Cholas, Kona Haihayas, Matsyas, Pusapati and others

accepted.s: Which ruler is associated with the Pithapuram inscription that mentions Kolleru Lake?
accepted.x: The Pithapuram inscription is associated with Velanati Prithvisvara. It mentions Kolleru Lake.
accepted.tq: Identify the ruler from the inscription-place association without confusing nearby minor dynasties.

accepted.s: Draksharama, also known as Jananathapura, is described in the inscriptions as the coronation seat of which of the following?
accepted.x: The Draksharama inscription identifies the place as the coronation seat of a Chalukya-Chola viceroy.
accepted.tq: Use the place–office association and avoid swapping rulers of neighbouring minor dynasties.

accepted.s: The Satrasala inscription is known as the founder’s record of which ruler?
o: Betaraju I of the Palnadu Haihayas
Manumasiddi I of the Nellore Chodas
accepted.x: The Satrasala inscription is the founder’s record of Palnadu Haihaya Betaraju I.
accepted.tq: Match the inscription with the ruler by focusing on the distinctive description ‘founder’s record’.

accepted.s: Which inscription praises Nellore Choda Manumasiddi I as a thunderbolt to his enemies?
accepted.x: The Taruvariyur inscription praises Nellore Choda Manumasiddi I as a thunderbolt to his enemies.
accepted.tq: Directly link the ruler’s epithet-like description with the correct inscriptional site.

accepted.s: The Kalamalla inscription, dated to 575 CE, is associated with which ruler?
accepted.x: The Kalamalla inscription of 575 CE is associated with Renati Choda Dhanunjaya.
accepted.tq: Use the date as an anchor to distinguish the two Renati Choda rulers.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Potladurthi is associated with Renati Choda Punyakumara. Kalamalla belongs to Dhanunjaya, Satrasala to Betaraju I, and Taruvariyur to Manumasiddi I.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure place–ruler pair and eliminate swapped inscription associations.

accepted.s: Amaravati, also known as Dhanyakatakam, and Tripurantakam lay in the territory of which dynasty?
accepted.x: Both Amaravati (Dhanyakatakam) and Tripurantakam lay in Kota territory.
accepted.tq: Test the territorial association while distinguishing a dynasty’s territory from an inscriptional ruler.

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the political structure of post-Eastern Chalukya Andhra?
o: It was governed by hereditary Kota rulers without subordinate nadus.
It was divided exclusively among independent Telugu Choda chiefs who rejected all overlordship.
It consisted of a web of nadus under vassals who accepted Velanadu and later Kakatiya overlordship when those powers were strong.
It was organised as a single centralised empire directly administered by the Chalukyas.
accepted.x: Post-Eastern Chalukya Andhra was a web of nadus under vassals. These vassals accepted Velanadu and subsequently Kakatiya overlordship when the respective power was strong.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that preserves the sequence of subordinate nadus and changing overlordship.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Velanati Chodas:
1. They were related to the Telugu Chodas.
2. Their ancestors were Kirtipura lords of Madhyadesha.
3. Their ancestry is distinct from that of the Telugu Chodas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statement 1 is false: the Velanati Chodas were not related to the Telugu Chodas. Statements 2 and 3 are correct; their ancestors were Kirtipura lords of Madhyadesha and their ancestry was distinct from that of the Telugu Chodas.
accepted.tq: Separate the confusable dynastic names before evaluating the ancestry statements.
